title: Press a stencil flat with one hand while the other dabs paint through its three holes
instruction: Press the stencil flat on the paper with one hand; with the other take the sponge dauber from its holder and dab it down through each of the stencil's three holes, once each, then lift it clear.
context: Stencilling (on signs, crates, walls, fabric or in a craft class) always takes two hands: one keeps the stencil flat and still against the surface while the other dabs the paint through it. A stencil that is not held lifts at its edges and the paint bleeds under it.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed sheet of white paper (120 g/m²), 20 x 30 cm, its long side across the table, centred 30 cm forward on the centre line. (2) A loose light-blue PET-plastic stencil, 12 g, 10 x 27 cm and 2 mm thick, lying across the paper 30 cm forward, from 13 cm right of the centre line to 14 cm left of it. Three square holes 3 cm across go through its right part, in a row, their middles 10.5, 6.7 and 2.9 cm right of the centre line. (3) A sponge dauber, 20 g: a yellow polyurethane sponge pad 1.8 cm square and 1 cm tall, inked red, under a wooden handle 1.4 cm square and 7.5 cm tall, standing upright in a square plastic holder 20 cm forward and 12 cm right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. A dab: the pad comes down onto the paper (within 1 mm of it, which it can only do through a hole) after being lifted at least 1 cm off it; it prints a square where it is. Held flat: at that moment the other gripper's fingertip centre (TCP) is on the stencil, within 3 cm above it; dabbed without the stencil held, the paint bleeds under it and the print is smudged (3.4 cm wide). 1.0: each of the three squares printed cleanly, once each (a clean print inside its hole where the stencil first lay, and exactly three prints in all), no smudged print, and the dauber lifted 1 cm off the paper; 0.5: two squares printed cleanly, or three prints with some smudged; 0.25: at least one print; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with the dauber and the stencil still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Put in a fresh sheet of paper, lay the stencil back across it, re-ink the dauber's sponge and stand it in its holder.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the paint is squares the task file lays on the paper where the pad comes down on it, one per dab. Paint bleeding under an unheld stencil is not simulated: the score counts a print dabbed without the stencil held as smudged and lays it wider. The sponge is rigid. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
